title_en: Interim Measures for the Examination of First-Appointed Judges and Assistant Judges of the Supreme People's Court
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Interim Measures for the Examination of First-Instance Judges and Assistant Judges

Fa Fa [1999] No. 18

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court on June 26, 1996; revised by the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court on June 15, 1999)

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of fairly selecting outstanding talents with both political integrity and professional competence, and building a contingent of judges who are politically steadfast, honest and upright, proficient in law, and impartial in law enforcement.

Article 2 Persons seeking initial appointment as first-instance judges or assistant judges must pass a unified national examination.

When an assistant judge is appointed to the judicial post of first-instance judge or above, no further examination is required.

Chapter II Examination Organization

Article 3 The Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court is the competent authority for organizing the unified national examination for first-instance judges and assistant judges. It is responsible for formulating the examination plan and organizing the implementation of the unified national examination.

Article 4 The Judges' Appraisal Committees of local people's courts at various levels and of special people's courts are responsible for organizing and implementing the examination within their respective jurisdictions, and shall undertake examination work entrusted by the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the superior people's court.

Article 5 The Judges' Appraisal Committee of each people's court shall establish an examination office during the period of the unified examination for first-instance judges and assistant judges, which shall be specifically responsible for the organization and implementation of the examination.

Chapter III Eligibility and Conditions for Applicants

Article 6 Eligible applicants:

Personnel of people's courts, lawyers, law teachers, and other legal professionals.

Article 7 Persons who register for the examination must meet the following conditions:

(1) possess the nationality of the People's Republic of China;

(2) have reached the age of twenty-three;

(3) uphold the Constitution of the People's Republic of China;

(4) have good political and professional qualities and good conduct;

(5) be in good health;

(6) have graduated from a college or university with a diploma in law and have been engaged in legal work for at least two years; have graduated from a university with a bachelor's degree in law or have obtained a bachelor's degree in law, or have graduated from a university with a bachelor's degree in a non-law field or have obtained a non-law bachelor's degree but possess legal expertise, and have been engaged in legal work for at least one year; holders of a master's or doctoral degree in law are not subject to the work experience requirement;

(7) other conditions prescribed by the Supreme People's Court and the high people's courts.

Chapter IV Examination Methods

Article 8 The Judges' Appraisal Committee of each people's court is responsible for the examination administration work within its region or unit, including registration, qualification review, examination room setup, invigilation, and the like.

Article 9 The main contents of the examination include legal knowledge and comprehensive knowledge.

The specific content of the examination shall be based on the examination review outline.

Article 10 The examination shall be conducted in two forms: a closed-book written examination and an oral examination. Only those who pass the written examination may participate in the oral examination.

Article 11 The examination review outline, questions, and grading criteria shall be formulated by the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 12 The grading work shall be organized and implemented uniformly by the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 13 For judicial personnel of the people's court who pass the examination, and for lawyers, law teachers, and other legal professionals who pass the examination and are transferred to work in a people's court, the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court, or a high people's court Judges' Appraisal Committee authorized thereby, shall issue the "Certificate of Qualification for the First-Instance Judge and Assistant Judge Examination."

Article 14 Persons who have obtained the "Certificate of Qualification for the First-Instance Judge and Assistant Judge Examination" may be appointed as judges as required by work needs.

Article 15 The "Certificate of Qualification for the First-Instance Judge and Assistant Judge Examination" shall be uniformly produced by the Supreme People's Court.

Chapter V Examination Discipline

Article 16 Examination disciplines, including rules for the examination room, invigilation regulations, and provisions on the confidentiality of examination papers, shall be formulated by the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 17 Persons who violate examination discipline shall be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions, depending on the severity of the circumstances.

Article 18 If a person has obtained the "Certificate of Qualification for the First-Instance Judge and Assistant Judge Examination" through cheating, the Judges' Appraisal Committee of the Supreme People's Court, or a high people's court Judges' Appraisal Committee authorized thereby, shall declare it invalid and retrieve the certificate.

Chapter VI Supplementary Provisions

Article 19 Examination funds shall be included in the court's operational expenses and used exclusively for that purpose. Examination registration fees collected in accordance with the provisions shall be entirely used for examination expenditures.

Article 20 The Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for the interpretation of these Measures.

Article 21 These Measures shall come into effect as of the date of promulgation.

June 22, 1999
